title: Unauthenticated Time-Blind SQLi in a WP-Style Slider Plugin
learning_objectives: Reach an unauthenticated admin-ajax action and recognise pre-auth attack surface in a WordPress-style plugin
Spot the wpdb->prepare() footgun: a query string built by concatenation with no %d/%s placeholder is NOT parameterised
Read data through a pure time-based oracle when the response body and status never vary with the payload
Bypass a CRS-baseline SQLi filter with inline-comment obfuscation (SLEEP/**/() and hex string literals (0x61646d696e) instead of quoted comments
Optimise extraction under a per-IP rate limiter with binary search parallelised across character positions
Understand why the recovered wp_users.user_pass is a 16-hex token here (not a 34-char phpass hash) so the automated exploit clears the <60s gate — the technique is identical at any length
flag_hint: POST /solve with JSON {"hash":"<16-hex>"} matching wp_users.user_pass for user_login='admin' returns the flag read from the flag file; any other value yields HTTP 403.
inspired_by: CVE-2024-2879 LayerSlider unauthenticated SQL Injection (abstracted; original plugin code not reproduced)
